scenes.audio: Marcus wants to reduce his insurance costs.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: Static graphic with a beige background. A teal header bar contains company branding. A single white box labeled 'Misrepresentation' appears on the left.

scenes.audio: A producer says a new policy has identical benefits,
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A second box labeled 'Twisting' slides in next to the first box. The overall lighting is flat and digital.

scenes.audio: but hides a shorter guarantee and a new surrender charge.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A third box labeled 'Proper comparison' appears on the right. Three distinct white rectangles are now visible across the frame.

scenes.audio: Misrepresentation means giving a false or misleading account of the policy.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The 'Misrepresentation' box is highlighted with a teal border. Text descriptions appear within the box.

scenes.audio: Twisting involves misleading statements or incomplete comparisons intended to induce a policy decision such as surrender, exchange, or lapse.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The highlight shifts to the 'Twisting' box. Bulleted points are added under the heading.

scenes.audio: Maryland's rule also covers inducing someone to retain a policy through that conduct.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The layout remains static while the audio continues describing regional legal specifics. Minimalist icons are used for branding at the bottom left.

scenes.audio: An honest, complete comparison can support a legitimate replacement. A replacement is not automatically twisting. Deception is the issue.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The highlight shifts to 'Proper comparison'. Text within the box clarifies the difference between replacement and twisting.

scenes.audio: Elena hears another agency
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The screen refreshes with a new header title. A single box for 'Defamation' appears.

scenes.audio: repeat a false claim that an insurer is insolvent.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A second box for 'False records' is added to the center of the beige canvas.

scenes.audio: Insurance defamation includes a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurer's financial condition... Altering records is not sales enthusiasm. Use verifiable facts.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Boxes for Defamation, False Records, and Accurate Comparison are highlighted sequentially. Text points populate each box as they are discussed.

scenes.audio: A producer offers to return part of a life premium personally if Aisha buys today.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Screen updates with header about inducements. Box for 'Off-contract rebate' appears on left.

scenes.audio: An off-contract premium rebate used to induce the sale can violate Maryland law.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Box for 'Specified materials' appears in the center.

scenes.audio: The state permits promotional materials costing no more than $50, but receipt cannot depend on buying insurance... A low dollar amount alone does not authorize a reward.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A third box for 'Purchase condition' is added. Each box is highlighted to explain the $50 limit and anti-rebate rules.

scenes.audio: Unfair discrimination is not the same as every difference in premium.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Title changes to Fair Treatment. Box for 'Comparable applicants' appears.

scenes.audio: Maryland prohibits unfair differences among life insurance applicants
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Box for 'Risk classification' appears next to the first box.

scenes.audio: Legitimate underwriting differences must respect statutory protections... The life statute has rules for blindness, hearing impairment, and genetic traits. Do not use stereotypes.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A third box for 'Protected circumstances' appears. Highlighted text lists specific traits like blindness and hearing impairment.

scenes.audio: Suppose a lender says Elena may obtain a loan only if she buys insurance through a chosen producer.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Title changes to Pressure. Three boxes labeled 01, 02, and 03 appear with arrows between them.

scenes.audio: Maryland prohibits tying access to credit to buying insurance through a particular producer... Another rule addresses concerted boycott or intimidation. Look for actual pressure.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The boxes fill with text regarding legitimate need, free choice, and prohibited pressure. Arrows indicate the flow of legal logic.

scenes.audio: A receptionist without a producer license can connect a customer with a licensed producer.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Title changes to Referrals and forms. Four numbered boxes (01-04) appear in a vertical stack.

scenes.audio: That does not authorize the receptionist to recommend policy terms... Do not ask a client to sign a blank application. Complete the facts accurately and obtain signatures.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The boxes for Referral, Compensation, Application, and Correction are highlighted. Each box displays compliance text.
